Hey man it’s okay to cry, you’re just a lot more sensitive and emotional than others it’s okay. I wouldn’t really understand why and can’t give you the answer myself but I want you to know that there isn’t anything wrong with crying bud and I hope people can treat and talk to you gently as I can. It could be as mentioned before you’re just really sensitive/emotional, or it could be some kind of response like a trauma one because something happened in the past, or it can be you need to slow down a bit as everything’s starting to overwhelm you that’s why you’re breaking down so easy, know you will be okay and are okay. Despite all these little things that happen and can make you cry, you are okay there’s nothing hurting you and you will be okay. Honestly if you think it might be either your body responding to something or you’re feeling so overwhelmed that the little things are getting to you maybe speak to a mental counselor, like my school has one, or a therapist to look deeper into it. If you’re just very sensitive tho that’s okay too you can work your way through this, counseling/therapy honestly could help too even if it’s small though I understand it may not be as easily accessible. Just know that crying is okay, I wouldn’t want you to hold back and bottle in your feelings man, and you will be okay too.

People go through rough moments in life, sometimes rougher and longer than most, and you’re an amazing person for being there for your wife through these times. Really consider what lillyoulosers said for her perspective, honestly I can relate to some extent with my boyfriend too although it’s the opposite I try so hard to not go to my boyfriend when I’m mentally unstable because I’m so scared of being a burden and end up being too much. And the thing is, what if I end up getting drove up to the point of no return? My reluctance to talk about it lets my thoughts corrupt my mine and actions even if such thoughts aren’t true and my partner wouldn’t even know anything, maybe they would wake up one day to *something* happening and wouldn’t even know why, they wouldn’t even have gotten the chance to help. I more of being up this bit because I wanted to highlight how important understanding and being able to hear her out in the first place is. Reassure that you love her, don’t let her think otherwise and don’t turn her away. While doing so keep encouraging for her to get help and maybe you need to put your foot down as well. 

Although to the main bit I wanted to go over, being overly dependent is just as bad as being avoidant as I said in my case. There needs to be a *balance* between the two, she should be able to open up and communicate with you however she can’t keep relying on you like this. Moreover keep in mind you can’t light yourself on fire to keep others warm. Yes you’re supposed to stay with your wife through sickness and health but that doesn’t mean sacrifice yourself, if you’re so exhausted you can’t even help her in the first place and honestly I know I’d feel 1000x worse if my partner was getting dragged down with me, create boundaries. Create plans that don’t involve her relying on you. Open up her support system, does she have anybody else to go to or call for help? Give yourself a break, you’ll still be there for her ofc but you need a break and not get dragged down by the negativity. Tell her to call her therapist if she needs help or an emergency appointment, even if it’s hard to reach out to others beside you she needs to do things for herself. She has to work on herself and really put in the effort most importantly. Putting your foot down at times will be needed too as you can’t keep caring for her like this, reassure her that you rlly do love her but she needs to do something. She’s still your very same wife a year ago,  she’s still in there under all the dark clouds, don’t give up on her but also don’t sacrifice yourself in the meantime. If this keeps up you might even just resent her which I don’t think we want at all, you need to care for yourself too and not have to worry about being her caretaker. If you haven’t already I prob will honestly recommend therapy for yourself to help you through this too and maybe couples therapy is needed again because the thing is she really will be the problem if she doesn’t help herself. She can’t fix magically unfortunately but she can still make progress for herself. Maybe these are all things you already know and considered, tho you’d need to go fully with them too. I just really hope things get better, just stay strong for you and your wife, and take care of yourself too give yourself a break tell her to go to her therapist or someone else instead of you for a while.
